messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Canary deploy `generator-v3` triggered alert (P1) in us-west-2. 429 error-rate > 7% and 5xx spike on /v1/generate over 3m. Auto-rollout pause suggested.
jess: picking this up. seeing large number of 429s and connection resets. traffic shifted ~12% to canary.
kai: looks like our client-side retry logic is amplifying 429s into cascades. also seeing sticky-session routing still sending to canary pods.
jess: can we flip the kill-switch flag `ff.generator_v3.enabled` -> false?
deploy-bot: kill-switch API acknowledged. Setting `ff.generator_v3.enabled=false` globally. Propagation to edge caches may take ~30s.
infra-ops: note: control-plane caches TTL=60s. flags applied to config-store but edge config pushed asynchronously.
jess: can't wait. plan B: scale canary down to 0 and drain pods. tara, can you scale? (cc @infra-ops)
infra-ops: scaling canary deployment `generator-v3-canary` to 0 replicas in us-west-2. command:```bash
kubectl -n models scale deploy generator-v3-canary --replicas=0 --region us-west-2
```
kai: doing that now. reminder: some long-lived websocket sessions are sticky; scaling to 0 will drop them and trigger reconnects.
sre-lead: acceptable tradeoff. notify support/CS for potential reconnects.
support-ops: posting status page update: "We are experiencing degraded generation responses in US West due to a canary rollback. Users may see failed requests or reconnects. Engineers are rolling back now."
jess: after scale started, 429s dropped from 7.8% -> 2.0% in 45s. still seeing intermittent 5xx from a small subset of hosts.
kai: discovered partial config drift: edge-proxy instances cached old routing to canary pods due to an intermittent push failure. I'll trigger a targeted restart of ingress sidecars in us-west-2 only.
infra-ops: restarting sidecars on ingress nodes (rolling, 1 at a time). command:```bash
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/ingress-sidecar -n infra --field-selector=metadata.labels.region=us-west-2
```
jess: heads-up: do not restart globally. only us-west-2.
support-ops: setting CS note to: "We've rolled back the canary and are restarting edge proxies; normal service expected within 10 minutes."
kai: ingress restart completed. rechecking metrics. 5xx now below baseline.
sre-lead: root-cause hypothesis so far: new request throttling behavior in generator-v3 combined with delayed edge flag propagation and sticky-session affinity caused retries and hot-path amplification -> 429/5xx cascade.
jess: followups: (1) add a pre-rollout step to invalidate edge caches post-flag flip, (2) add canary traffic guard that prevents >10% sticky-affecting sessions during model swaps, (3) add test for client retry/backoff resilience.
kai: I'll create the rollout guard ticket and own 2). jira: INFRA-9123.
infra-ops: investigating why edge push failed; logs show transient HTTP 502 when pushing config to proxy pool at ~21:10Z. opening infra incident INFRA-2345.
sre-lead: mitigation summary: 1) flipped feature flag off 2) scaled canary to 0 3) restarted ingress sidecars in region 4) updated support/status messages. Customer impact: ~5% of requests in us-west for ~8 minutes saw elevated failures, a few short-lived reconnects for websocket clients.
jess: handing off to next oncall (kai) for 60m watch. notes: watch for residual 429s and make sure INFRA-2345 doesn't lead to config push regressions elsewhere.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1761118400: paging -> handoff. next oncall: kai.
kai: acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor and follow infra incident.
support-ops: two customer tickets opened: C-10021, C-10022. notifying affected tenants.
sre-lead: postmortem owners: jess (draft), infra-ops (edge push reliability fix), eng-client (retry/backoff improvement). Please tag P0 for rollout guard.
jess: starting postmortem now. timeline + metrics + exact commands will be added.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED 1761119000: Pager closed. Follow-ups required: postmortem, rollout-playbook updates, edge push retry hardening.
kai: thanks team. :thumbsup: closing thread.
